articleSummary: New travel-related dengue case identified on Kauaʻi, Hawaii, bringing statewide 2026 total to five; patient recently returned from international travel to a dengue-transmission area and has no identified link to prior Hawaii cases. Hawaiʻi Department of Health (DOH) deployed vector-control teams to inspect the affected area, implement mosquito-reduction measures, and provide outreach materials. Transmission risk is considered low given the travel-associated nature of the case, but upcoming storms may boost mosquito populations. Dengue is not endemic in Hawaiʻi and current cases are travel-associated. Dengue is a year-round risk in tropical/subtropical regions worldwide, including Central/South America (Brazil, Mexico), Asia (Philippines), the Caribbean (Puerto Rico), and Pacific Islands (American Samoa, FSM, Marshall Islands, Palau). Travelers should use EPA-registered repellent, wear long sleeves/pants, and stay in screened or air-conditioned spaces; return travelers should guard against bites for three weeks and seek evaluation if fever or dengue-like symptoms appear within two weeks. Symptoms include fever, nausea, vomiting, rash, and body aches; most recover within about a week.

articleSummary: Roche Diagnostics Korea introduces cobas Malaria PCR testing at Hanmaeum Blood Center, the nation’s first implementation of malaria nucleic acid testing (NAT) on all donated blood. The novel FMDV is a positive-sense single-stranded RNA virus, less stable than African swine fever virus, mainly affecting cattle and sheep; infections in pigs are rare. Domestic cattle and sheep herds total about 100 million and 280 million, respectively, with Xinjiang, Gansu, and Ningxia accounting for roughly 16% of national cattle. The outbreak may drive herd culling and lift beef prices, while hog farming remains less affected but boosts investment sentiment.

articleSummary: As of 10 April 2026, all 40 schistosomiasis-endemic counties/cities/districts in Hunan Province, China, have met the elimination standard. articleSummary: Cat bites are not minor: CDC notes 20–80% of cat bites or scratches become infected. The primary offender is Pasteurella multocida, present in 70–90% of cats and found in about 75% of bite wounds. Infections usually appear within 24–48 hours with pain, swelling, redness, and inflammation, and may progress to cellulitis or abscess; sepsis is rare. Bites can also transmit other diseases, including cat scratch disease (Bartonella henselae) with fever and lymphadenopathy 1–3 weeks after exposure; rabies risk remains, especially from wild cats; tetanus risk; and, rarely, sporotrichosis. Initial care: wash the wound with running water and soap for at least 5 minutes, do not seal the wound, and seek medical care promptly. Seek medical attention if the wound is deep, hard to clean, red, swollen, painful, feverish, rabies status unknown, or tetanus vaccine >5 years old. Antibiotics can treat most cases.

articleSummary: As of 10 April 2026 (week 12 of 2026), Central Sulawesi, Indonesia reported 895 suspected measles cases across multiple districts, led by Palu City with 542 cases, followed by Sigi Regency (112), Donggala Regency (89), and Tojo Una-Una Regency (68); cases are spread in several districts with remaining cases in other areas. Most cases are in infants, though under-9-month-olds retain maternal antibodies and are generally protected. Measles vaccination remains logistically feasible; health authorities say all under-five targets can be vaccinated and there are no logistical constraints. Transmission may be due to external sources or reduced immunity, and not all suspected cases qualify as a KLB (measles outbreak). Interventions and specimen transport are coordinated by district/city health offices.

articleSummary: Cholera is not solely sourced from Bangladesh; a genomic study challenges the long-held view that the Ganges Delta is the main hub of modern cholera. The analysis indicates the principal engine of global spread lies in the broader Ganges basin and India, which appear to export Vibrio cholerae lineages to other regions. Researchers sequenced more than 2,300 Vibrio cholerae genomes from Bangladesh and northern India, identifying shared ancestries and transmission patterns that implicate the wider basin rather than a single country as the primary source. The findings imply that international public health surveillance should consider cross-border spread within the Ganges system. The report does not present outbreak counts, but underscores the role of genomic surveillance in tracing introductions of cholera strains worldwide.

articleHeadline: Computational identification of conserved dengue virus envelope protein epitopes for vaccine design and immunodiagnostic platform - Scientific Reports
articleSummary: Global dengue remains a major health challenge with more than 390 million infections annually across four serotypes (DENV1-4). In silico analysis of the dengue virus envelope (E) protein identified conserved CD8+ and CD4+ T-cell epitopes across serotypes, supporting potential universal vaccine design, alongside distinct serotype-specific epitopes for precise immunodiagnostics (notably for DENV-2, DENV-3, and DENV-4). Molecular docking revealed strong peptide-HLA binding with favorable energies, exemplified by LTDYGALTL-HLA-A01:01 and DTAWDFGSI-HLA-A26:01, while normal mode analysis indicated stability of the epitope-HLA complexes. Intrinsically disordered regions of the E protein were analyzed to locate flexible segments relevant to immune recognition. Population coverage is estimated at 66.87% globally, with higher representation in East Asia, Europe, and the Americas. Collectively, the framework informs next-generation multivalent dengue vaccines and serotype-specific diagnostic platforms.

articleSummary: Measles is entering a period of high incidence, with China facing substantial imported infection risk, according to Nanchang City CDC. articleHeadline: ¿Qué es el Nodavirus de Mortalidad Encubierta? El virus marino vinculado a infecciones oculares graves en humanos
articleSummary: CMNV, the Hidden Mortality Nodavirus, previously confined to marine aquaculture, has been linked to severe ocular infections in humans in China. A Nature Communications study led by University College London confirms human involvement through genomic analysis showing a 98.96% match between the virus in patients and marine isolates, establishing a marine origin. The infection associates with anterior viral hypertensive persistent ocular uveitis (POH-VAU), an inflammation of the eye’s front segment with chronically elevated intraocular pressure that can irreversibly damage the optic nerve and cause complete vision loss. Reported symptoms include intense eye pain, redness, photophobia, blurred vision, and floaters; notable absence of respiratory symptoms may hinder early detection. Transmission appears linked to handling and consumption of infected seafood, with over 70% of cases recalling contact with raw fish or shellfish. Preventive measures emphasize fully cooking seafood, strict hand hygiene after handling, and gloves if hands are injured during fish cleaning.

articleHeadline: 注意！蚊子提前"上班"，这两种"热病"正悄悄北上
articleSummary: Two mosquito-borne diseases—dengue fever and chikungunya fever—are moving north in China as spring warms. The primary vector is Aedes albopictus (white-striped mosquito), thriving near homes in clean standing-water containers. Dengue causes abrupt high fever (39–40°C) lasting 2–7 days, with severe headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgias, rash and potential vomiting. Chikungunya features intense multi-joint pain (hands, wrists, knees, ankles) with fever and rash; joint symptoms can be prolonged and disabling. Historically endemic in Guangdong, Yunnan, Hainan, Guangxi, these diseases now show locally transmitted cases in northern provinces: Shandong, Henan, Shaanxi, Hebei, Beijing, Tianjin. Transmission occurs via mosquito bites, not human-to-human spread; imported cases from the south or Southeast Asia can seed local chains. Preventive guidance: seek prompt care with travel/exposure history; avoid NSAIDs in suspected dengue; use repellents, long sleeves, bed nets, and screens; monitor health for two weeks after travel.
notes: 記事は中国におけるデング熱とチクングニア熱の北上傾向を報告。従来は南部（広東、雲南、海南、広西）に限定されていた疾患が、山東、河南、陕西、河北、北京、天津などの北部地域で局所伝播例が確認されている。Aedes albopictus（ヒトスジシマカ）が媒介生物。蚊媒介感染症の地理的拡大はWPRO地域における公衆衛生上の重要なシグナルである。

articleHeadline: Altering HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein maturation and its effects on viral infectivity
articleSummary: HIV-1 relies on envelope glycoprotein Env maturation for infectivity. Treatment of HIV-1–infected cells with the tri-peptide GPG-NH2 reduces virion infectivity by impairing Env maturation and incorporation. GPG-NH2 decreases Env steady-state levels and processing to gp120/gp41 and causes a downshift in Env mass due to deglycosylation, targeting Env for ERAD. The effect depends on metabolism via G-NH2 to the active metabolite ?HGA, generated in fetal bovine serum-containing cultures; in human serum or serum-free media, only ?HGA drives Env destruction. The native 30-residue Env signal sequence governs gp160 ER targeting; surprisingly, its first 8 residues are dispensable for gp160 expression but regulate Env content in particles. Wild-type virus incorporates ~80% more gp160 and ~20% less gp120/gp41 than the 8-residue-truncated signal sequence virus, leading to ~40% reduction in infectivity. Overall, altering Env content and maturation via small-molecule modulation can substantially affect HIV-1 infectivity, suggesting therapeutic potential.

articleSummary: Black Death (1346–1353) killed about half the population in affected areas, 100 million people, and was global, spreading from Sicily to Egypt, France, Syria, Spain, Sweden, and Russia. Demographic shocks appear in Africa (Ghana, Nigeria, Burkina Faso) and Tunisia; Ibn Khaldun survived, and plagues helped shape civilizations. The historian underscores micro-histories, such as Princess Joan of England, who died at 14 after contracting plague in Bordeaux; many nobles and commoners perished. Without germ theory, contemporaries reacted with shock, and some blamed groups, fueling anti-Jewish massacres in towns across France, Basel, and the Iberian Peninsula. Notaries continued work; Florence and Bologna show spikes in wills, signaling impending death. The plague persisted as an endemic in London (1665) and elsewhere, contributing to feudal decline and possibly accelerating changes in Constantinople and the Reformation. Madagascar outbreaks in 2014 and 2017 caused ~300 deaths. Pandemics leave social and political legacies, prompting reflections on COVID-19.

articleHeadline: Study highlights long-term neurologic impacts of Nipah infection
articleSummary: Nipah virus survivors experience substantial long-term neurologic deficits and fatigue. articleSummary: Lassa fever in Nigeria: The death toll has risen to 167 this year, with an ongoing outbreak across multiple states as of January 2026. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) reports confirmed cases have declined from 51 to 26 in the latest update, yet fatalities continue to rise. The disease, transmitted to humans via rodent droppings and capable of human-to-human spread, causes a deadly hemorrhagic fever. The outbreak remains widespread, affecting rural areas and other regions nationwide. Nigeria previously declared a national emergency related to Lassa fever on January 23, 2019; in 2025 the country recorded 190 deaths. Lassa fever has also been observed in several West African countries including Mali, Togo, Ghana, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Public health authorities urge reducing contact with rodents to curb transmission.

articleSummary: Measles remains highly contagious in Jakarta, Indonesia, with officials noting a downward trend in overall cases, but a single school case requires strict containment. articleHeadlineTranslated: CMNV nodavirus, the marine virus that can cause blindness in humans.
articleHeadline: Nodavirus CMNV, el virus marino que puede causar ceguera en humanos
articleSummary: CMNV nodavirus (Covert Mortality Nodavirus) is linked to a human ocular disease for the first time. In March 2026, Nature Microbiology reported an association between CMNV and Anterior Viral Uveitis with Persisting Ocular Hypertension (POH-VAU) in China, analyzing 70 patients and identifying ocular tissues with ~99% genetic similarity to aquatic CMNV strains; infection reproduced in mouse models, supporting causality. CMNV, a non-enveloped single-stranded RNA virus in Nodaviridae, has a two-segment genome and is highly environmentally stable in water, sediments, and aquaculture systems, enabling persistence and spread. In shrimp, CMNV can cause up to 80% mortality. Human exposure appears linked to direct contact with raw seafood or handling aquaculture products, with entry through skin micro-lesions or mucous membranes, especially the eyes. No evidence of person-to-person transmission; cases centered in China and parts of Asia. Mexico (SENASICA) monitors CMNV; Colombia and other Latin American shrimp industries are urged to strengthen biosafety.
notes: 記事サマリーではCMNVと人間の眼病（POH-VAU）の関連が中国で初めて報告されたと述べられている。メキシコとコロンビアは監視・対応国として言及されているが、実際のイベント発生地は中国に限定される。水産業・食品安全に関わる新規病原体であり、食料チェーンを通じた国際的な波及リスクがある。Nature Microbiologyでの発表により学術的な可信性が高い。

articleHeadlineTranslated: Fruits that children with hand, foot and mouth disease should eat.
articleHeadline: Nhóm trái cây trẻ mắc bệnh tay chân miệng nên ăn
articleSummary: Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease (HFMD) is an acute contagious enterovirus infection. In Vietnam, parents are advised to support recovery with soft, watery fruits rich in antioxidants and vitamin C, while avoiding highly acidic citrus (orange, grapefruit, lemon) to minimize mouth irritation. Early HFMD can cause mouth ulcers and dehydration; recommended fruits include watermelon, cantaloupe, banana, avocado, papaya, grapes, dragon fruit, strawberries, blueberries, and ripe pear. These provide fiber, vitamins A/C/E, potassium, and hydration, potentially reducing oral discomfort. Preparation options: smoothies (banana, avocado, papaya, dragon fruit) with milk/yogurt or honey; diluted fruit juice; steaming or simmering to soften; soft jelly. Practice good hygiene: wash fruits, peel/remove seeds, clean utensils. Distribute fruit portions across the day and avoid overly cold items. HFMD usually resolves in 7–10 days; seek care for fever ≥39 C, lethargy, persistent crying, seizures, breathing difficulties, or blue discoloration.

articleHeadline: Two new vaccines show promise in tackling TB, especially among kids
articleSummary: Two new vaccines, VPM1002 (genetically modified recombinant BCG by Serum Institute of India, Pune) and Immuvac (Cadila), show promise against TB in a BMJ study published April 9. VPM1002 showed 50.4% effectiveness against extrapulmonary TB (EPTB) overall and 79.5% in 36–60-year-olds; Immuvac showed 66.3% efficacy against EPTB in latent TB and over 60% against EPTB in 6–10-year-olds. Across groups, VPM1002 provided about 60% efficacy against all TB, PTB and EPTB in 6–14 years; Immuvac about 60% against EPTB in 6–10 years. EPTB accounts for roughly 22% of India’s TB cases and affects lymph nodes, pleura, abdomen and spine. Neither vaccine offered general protection or prevented latent infection; protection from latent TB at 6 months was noted. Underweight individuals remained unprotected, underscoring the need for nutrition and housing improvements alongside vaccination.

articleSummary: Nipah virus outbreak in Kampung Sungai Nipah (Sungai Nipah New Village) near Port Dickson, Negeri Sembilan, Malaysia, began during the Lunar New Year, lasting about a month and killing more than 109 people. Authorities culled over 1.16 million pigs; villagers were evacuated and pigs buried in pits. Twenty-seven years on (2026), survivor Lin Jianmin recalls the trauma and the collapse of pig farming, with many families later finding work at Kuala Lumpur International Airport and in duty-free shops. A Nipah Time Tunnel Museum, opened in 2018, documents the events. The village traces to 1952 under British colonial policy forming a “New Village”; pig farming once thrived before the 1998–1999 Nipah outbreak shut the industry and spurred diversification. The piece also notes an earlier Nipah outbreak in West Bengal this year as a global health alert.
notes: 記事サマリーは主にマレーシアの1998-1999年の歴史的ニパウイルスアウトブレイク（27年前）の回想記事であり、現在のアクティブな脅威は西ベンガル州での本年の発生のみ言及されている。マレーシアは対象国リストに含まれていないため verified_locations には含めない。IHR基準を2つ満たしており、WPROスクリーニング基準を3つ満たしているが、記事の主要内容が過去のイベント回想であることから WATCH 判定とした。西ベンガル州での2026年の発生の詳細情報が不足しているため、続報の注視が必要。

articleHeadline: Lonjakan Kasus Campak di Indonesia, Ancaman Nyata yang Tak Pandang Usia
articleSummary: Measles cases surge in Indonesia, signaling a threat beyond childhood. WHO ranks Indonesia second worldwide for measles in 2025 with 17,204 confirmed cases, a pattern continuing into 2026. Indonesia’s Ministry of Health, through week 8 of 2026, reports 8,372 confirmed cases and 10,453 suspected. Measles is a highly contagious airborne infection; a single case can transmit to up to 18 susceptible people, and the virus can linger in air or on surfaces for up to two hours after the patient leaves. Without vaccination, measles can cause pneumonia, encephalitis, and death. Transmission is facilitated in crowded closed spaces like public transport and classrooms. A major concern is immune amnesia: 11–73% of the antibody memory bank may be erased after infection, leaving recovered individuals vulnerable to other diseases. Dr. Nina Dwi Putri notes severe complications can occur even in adults; a young doctor’s death is suspected due to measles.
notes: 記事はインドネシアでの麻疹流行を主題とし、WHO報告（2025年17,204例、2026年継続増加）、インドネシア保健省の公式データ（8,372確定例、10,453疑い例）を引用。高い伝播性（感染者1人が最大18人に感染）、免疫記憶喪失による免疫低下、成人死亡例の報告、肺炎・脳炎などの重症合併症が複数記載されており、公衆衛生上の重大な脅威と判断される。

articleSummary: China researchers investigating a rise in an unusual ocular disease have found evidence linking a marine Nodavirus (CMNV) to a chronic viral anterior uveitis with persistent ocular hypertension (POH-VAU) in humans. In a study of 70 POH-VAU patients diagnosed 2022–2025, viral particles were detected in ocular tissues, with immunological markers specific to CMNV and genetic analysis showing ~99% similarity to CMNV strains from aquatic animals. The team notes that most affected individuals reported frequent exposure to raw seafood or handling of seafood without protective gear, suggesting a zoonotic transmission route. Experimental work in cell cultures and mice reproduced features including ocular inflammation and elevated intraocular pressure, supporting a potential causal role for CMNV. The virus appears not geographically restricted, found in multiple marine species (crabs, mollusks) across continents. Findings published in Nature Microbiology; highlighted by MedicalXpress; emphasize seafood safety and ongoing surveillance for emergent zoonoses.
notes: 海洋性ノダウイルス（CMNV）による新規人獣共通感染症の確認。2022-2025年に70例の患者が確認され、実験的検証も実施済み。記事サマリーはNature Microbiologyへの発表を示唆しており、学術的信頼性が高い。海産物の安全性に関連し、貿易・渡航規制のリスクあり。ウイルスが多大陸にわたる海洋生物から検出される可能性がある点は国際的拡大リスクを示唆。

articleHeadline: Cà Mau: 3 trường hợp nghi viêm não mô cầu, 1 người đã tử vong
articleSummary: On 11 April 2026, Ca Mau Provincial Center for Disease Control reported three suspected meningococcal meningitis cases in Hamlet 6, Khanh An Commune, Ca Mau Province. All three had contact with a person who died in March 2026 after fever, petechiae, and hypotension. Case 1: admitted 7 April with petechiae, vomiting, lethargy; fever of unknown origin; meningitis/sepsis suspected; blood sample sent to Pasteur Institute, Ho Chi Minh City. Case 2: admitted 8 April with high fever and altered mental status; died 9 April; diagnosed as septic shock from gastrointestinal infection with multiple comorbidities; samples collected for etiologic testing. Case 3: transferred 9 April after prolonged fever, cough, myalgia, hypotension and pleural effusion; fever with skin hemorrhages; initially managed as sepsis, dengue fever, and pneumonia; CSF and blood sent for testing. No additional suspected cases reported at investigation time; local authorities implementing outbreak controls.
notes: 記事サマリーには古典的豚熱(Classical Swine Fever)の言及は見当たらない。Bluedotが複数疾患を抽出しているが、主要な公衆衛生上の懸念は髄膜炎菌性髄膜炎である。デング熱との鑑別診断も記載されているが、髄膜炎菌性髄膜炎の可能性が中心。Ca Mau Provinceに限定した局地的クラスターであるが、死亡例を含む重症例が複数発生しており、急速な対応が必要。
